messages:
tara: Heads-up — dashboards are reporting LCP regressions and big main-thread spikes after last night's routing/prefetch rollout. Heatmap + metrics panels particularly bad. anyone else seeing this?

sam: +1. Looking at profiles now — main-thread parse up ~40% on canary. The telemetry bundle was pulled into the critical path by the new prefetch handshake.

oliver: I can repro locally when I flip on `PREFETCH_AFFINITY=aggressive`. CPU flame shows `telemetry-client` parse + `chart-worker` idle. Also seeing a lot more k/v prefetch traffic -> kvcache misses. link: http://perf.mock/reports/5112345678 (sanitized)

jenna: Repro steps I used: open /dashboards/overview (EU canary), clear cache, hit with 3 concurrent users. LCP jumps from ~800ms to ~2.2s. Console shows `telemetry:init` logged before any dynamic imports finish.

deploy-bot: deploy: routing-policy v2 rolled to canary (eu) — release id `rp-v2-2026-03-20-22` (deployed by @sam)

sam: Root cause hypothesis: routing-policy changed prefetch window + we defaulted telemetry to eager init on route entry. Two things combined: (1) telemetry import increased bundle parse, (2) kv prefetch concurrency increased contention causing main-thread queuing.

matt: Quick mitigation options: reduce prefetch concurrency + make telemetry a dynamic import on heavy routes. Also we can lower sampling on canary to reduce telemetry payload.

jenna: Agreed. I can push a small client patch to lazy-load telemetry and drop prefetch concurrency for EU. Would prefer a targeted canary rollback if that's faster.

oliver: If we do patch, here's the minimal change that should help (pseudo):

```
// lazy init telemetry
function maybeInitTelemetry() {
  if (!shouldSample()) return;
  import('./telemetry-client').then(mod => mod.init({sampleRate:0.05}));
}

// prefetch config tweak (env)
PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=2
PREFETCH_WINDOW_MS=150
```

sam: +1 on the patch. If rollback is faster though -> roll back `rp-v2-2026-03-20-22` in EU only, then iterate on the client patch. I can trigger a zone-limited rollback.

matt: Also suggest adding a temporary telemetry gate for heavy panels: `if (route.includes('heatmap')) skipTelemetry=true`. Ugly but buys time.

tara: Who can do the rollback now? @sam can you run it and I will coordinate observability thresholds to watch? p95 LCP, parse time, and kvcache miss rate.

sam: Starting rollback for EU canary now. I'll post status.

ci-bot: rollback job queued: job id `rb-511234-01`. ETA ~2m

jenna: I'll open a PR with the lazy-import + env tweaks and include a test harness to reproduce locally.

oliver: After rollback stabilizes, follow-ups: 1) revert the aggressive prefetch default, 2) add telemetry lazy-init RFC, 3) instrument per-route parse-time heatmaps.

tara: Thanks everyone. Priority: stabilize user-facing LCP, then land the telemetry lazy-load for a proper fix. :thumbsup:

sam: Rollback finished for EU canary — metrics trending back to baseline within 3 deployments. Monitoring for 30m.

jenna: PR created: #4821 — includes lazy import + prefetch env changes + repro script.

matt: Nice. After this we should also consider splitting telemetry into a small core + optional plugins so parse impact is predictable.

tara: Agreed. I'll schedule a short follow-up discussion tomorrow to decide rollout strategy and safeguards.

sam: Closing loop: leave routing-policy in staging until we have patch validated. Will post a postmortem if anything else pops up.
